fix msd_output all print 100 "${step} $(c_msd_compute[1]) $(c_msd_compute[2]) $(c_msd_compute[3]) $(c_msd_compute[4])" &
    file msd_data.txt screen no title "# Step MSD_x MSD_y MSD_z MSD_total"

run 500000

unfix equil_npt

print(f"MSD range: {msd[0]:.6f} to {msd[-1]:.6f} Angstrom^2")

skip_fraction = 0.1

D_m2_s = D_angstrom2_ps * 1e-8

    f.write(f"Slope: {slope:.6f} Angstrom^2/ps\n")
    f.write(f"R-squared: {r_value**2:.6f}\n")
    f.write(f"Data points used: {len(time_fit)}\n")
    f.write(f"Time range: {time_fit[0]:.3f} to {time_fit[-1]:.3f} ps\n")

print(f"\nResults saved to diffusion_coefficient.txt")

plt.plot(time, msd, 'b-', linewidth=0.5, alpha=0.7, label='MSD data')

plt.xlabel('Time (ps)', fontsize=12)
plt.ylabel('MSD (Angstrom²)', fontsize=12)
plt.title('Mean Squared Displacement vs Time\nLiquid Silicon at 2500K', fontsize=14)
plt.legend(fontsize=10)
plt.grid(True, alpha=0.3)

plt.savefig('msd_plot.png', dpi=150)
print("Plot saved to msd_plot.png")

print(f"\n{'='*60}")
print(f"FINAL RESULT: D = {D_m2_s:.6e} m^2/s")
print(f"{'='*60}")
"}</action_input>

# LAMMPS input script for melting silicon and calculating self-diffusion coefficient
# Task: Heat from 300K to 2500K at 2.2 K/ps, then equilibrate for 500 ps

# Initialization
units metal
atom_style full
boundary p p p

# Read structure and replicate
read_data si_structure.data
replicate 3 3 3

# Define potential - Stillinger-Weber for Si
pair_style sw
pair_coeff * * /potentials/SW/Si.sw Si

# Neighbor list settings
neighbor 1.0 bin
neigh_modify every 1 delay 0 check yes

# Timestep (1 fs)
timestep 0.001

# Thermodynamic output settings
thermo 1000
thermo_style custom step temp press density pe ke etotal vol

# Heating phase: 300K to 2500K at 2.2 K/ps (1000 ps = 1,000,000 steps)
velocity all create 300.0 12345 dist gaussian
fix heat_npt all npt temp 300.0 2500.0 0.1 iso 0.0 0.0 1.0
run 1000000
unfix heat_npt

# Equilibration phase at 2500K for 500 ps (500,000 steps)
# Reset time and compute MSD
reset_timestep 0

# Compute MSD for all atoms
compute msd_compute all msd com yes

# Fix for NPT equilibration
fix equil_npt all npt temp 2500.0 2500.0 0.1 iso 0.0 0.0 1.0

# Output MSD data
fix msd_output all print 1000 "$(step) $(c_msd_compute[1]) $(c_msd_compute[2]) $(c_msd_compute[3]) $(c_msd_compute[4])" file msd_data.txt screen no title "# Step MSD_x MSD_y MSD_z MSD_total"

# Run equilibration
run 500000

# Clean up
unfix equil_npt
unfix msd_output

print "Simulation completed successfully"

import pandas as pd
import numpy as np
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt

# Read the equilibration log
df = pd.read_csv('equilibration_log.csv')

# Extract time (in ps) and MSD (in Angstrom^2)
# Step is in timesteps, timestep = 0.001 ps
time_ps = df['Step'] * 0.001  # Convert to ps
msd_angstrom2 = df['c_msd[4]']  # MSD in Angstrom^2

print(f"Total data points: {len(df)}")
print(f"Time range: {time_ps.min():.2f} to {time_ps.max():.2f} ps")
print(f"MSD range: {msd_angstrom2.min():.6f} to {msd_angstrom2.max():.6f} Angstrom^2")

# Plot MSD vs time to visualize
plt.figure(figsize=(10, 6))
plt.plot(time_ps, msd_angstrom2, 'b-', linewidth=1)
plt.xlabel('Time (ps)')
plt.ylabel('MSD (Angstrom^2)')
plt.title('Mean Squared Displacement vs Time')
plt.grid(true)
plt.savefig('msd_vs_time.png', dpi=150)
plt.close()

print("\nMSD vs time plot saved as msd_vs_time.png")

# For diffusion coefficient calculation, we need the linear regime
# Typically, we skip the initial ballistic regime and use the later linear part
# Let's use data from 100 ps onwards to avoid initial transients

# Find indices where time >= 100 ps
mask = time_ps >= 100.0
time_linear = time_ps[mask].values
msd_linear = msd_angstrom2[mask].values

print(f"\nUsing data from {time_linear[0]:.2f} to {time_linear[-1]:.2f} ps for linear fit")
print(f"Number of points in linear regime: {len(time_linear)}")

# Perform linear fit: MSD = 6*D*t
# So D = slope / 6
coeffs = np.polyfit(time_linear, msd_linear, 1)
slope = coeffs[0]  # Angstrom^2 / ps
intercept = coeffs[1]

print(f"\nLinear fit results:")
print(f"Slope: {slope:.6f} Angstrom^2/ps")
print(f"Intercept: {intercept:.6f} Angstrom^2")

# Calculate diffusion coefficient
# D = slope / 6
# Units: Angstrom^2/ps = 10^-20 m^2 / 10^-12 s = 10^-8 m^2/s
D_angstrom2_per_ps = slope / 6.0
D_m2_per_s = D_angstrom2_per_ps * 1e-8  # Convert to m^2/s

print(f"\nDiffusion coefficient:")
print(f"D = {D_angstrom2_per_ps:.6f} Angstrom^2/ps")
print(f"D = {D_m2_per_s:.6e} m^2/s")

# Plot the linear fit
plt.figure(figsize=(10, 6))
plt.plot(time_ps, msd_angstrom2, 'b-', linewidth=1, label='MSD data')
plt.plot(time_linear, slope * time_linear + intercept, 'r--', linewidth=2, label=f'Linear fit (slope={slope:.4f})')

print(f"Time range: {time[0]:.3f} to {time[-1]:.3f} ps")
print(f"MSD range: {msd[0]:.6f} to {msd[-1]:.6f} Angstrom^2")

# For better statistics, use the linear regime (typically after initial transient)
# Skip the first 10% of data to avoid initial transient effects
skip_fraction = 0.1
skip_points = int(len(time) * skip_fraction)

time_fit = time[skip_points:]
msd_fit = msd[skip_points:]

print(f"\nUsing data from {time_fit[0]:.3f} to {time_fit[-1]:.3f} ps for fitting")
print(f"Number of points for fitting: {len(time_fit)}")

# Perform linear regression: MSD = 6*D*t
# slope = 6*D
slope, intercept, r_value, p_value, std_err = stats.linregress(time_fit, msd_fit)

print(f"\nLinear fit results:")
print(f"Slope: {slope:.6f} Angstrom^2/ps")
print(f"Intercept: {intercept:.6f} Angstrom^2")
print(f"R-squared: {r_value**2:.6f}")
print(f"Standard error: {std_err:.6e}")

print(f"\nDiffusion coefficient:")

D_m2_s = D_angstrom2_ps * 1e-8

# LAMMPS input script for silicon melting and diffusion coefficient calculation
# Task: Heat silicon from 300K to 2500K, equilibrate, and compute diffusion coefficient

# Initialization
units metal
atom_style full
boundary p p p

# Read structure and replicate
read_data si_structure.data
replicate 3 3 3

# Define potential (Stillinger-Weber)
pair_style sw
pair_coeff * * /potentials/SW/Si.sw Si

# Set neighbor list
neighbor 2.0 bin
neigh_modify every 1 delay 0 check yes

# Define compute for temperature
compute myTemp all temp

# Thermodynamic output settings
thermo 1000
thermo_style custom step temp press density pe ke etotal vol

# Stage 1: Initial energy minimization
min_style cg
minimize 1.0e-6 1.0e-8 10000 100000

# Reset timestep
reset_timestep 0

# Stage 2: Heating from 300K to 2500K at 2.2 K/ps
# Heating time: (2500-300)/2.2 = 1000 ps
# Timestep: 0.001 ps = 1 fs
timestep 0.001

# NPT ensemble for heating (zero pressure)
fix npt_heat all npt temp 300.0 2500.0 0.1 iso 0.0 0.0 1.0

# Run heating for 1000 ps = 1,000,000 steps
run 1000000

# Unfix heating
unfix npt_heat

# Reset timestep for equilibration
reset_timestep 0

# Stage 3: Equilibration at 2500K for 500 ps
fix npt_equil all npt temp 2500.0 2500.0 0.1 iso 0.0 0.0 1.0

# Run equilibration for 500 ps = 500,000 steps
run 500000

# Unfix equilibration
unfix npt_equil

# Reset timestep for MSD calculation
reset_timestep 0

# Stage 4: Production run for MSD calculation at 2500K
# Continue NPT at 2500K and compute MSD
fix npt_prod all npt temp 2500.0 2500.0 0.1 iso 0.0 0.0 1.0

# Compute MSD for all atoms
compute msd_all all msd com yes

# Output MSD data
fix msd_output all print 100 "$(step) $(c_msd_all[1]) $(c_msd_all[2]) $(c_msd_all[3]) $(c_msd_all[4])" file msd_data.txt screen no title "# Step MSD_x MSD_y MSD_z MSD_total"

run 500000

print "Simulation completed successfully"

import numpy as np
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
from scipy import stats

# Read MSD data
data = np.loadtxt('msd_data.txt', skiprows=2)

# Extract columns
timesteps = data[:, 0]  # timesteps
msd = data[:, 4]  # total MSD (4th column)

# Convert timesteps to time in picoseconds
# timestep = 0.001 ps, but data is output every 100 steps
dt = 0.001  # ps per timestep
time_ps = timesteps * dt  # time in ps

# For diffusion coefficient calculation, use the linear regime
# Typically after initial equilibration (use last 60-80% of data)
start_idx = int(0.3 * len(time_ps))  # Start from 30% to avoid initial transient
end_idx = len(time_ps)

time_fit = time_ps[start_idx:end_idx]
msd_fit = msd[start_idx:end_idx]

# Linear fit: MSD = 6Dt
# So slope = 6D, and D = slope/6
slope, intercept, r_value, p_value, std_err = stats.linregress(time_fit, msd_fit)

# Calculate diffusion coefficient
# MSD is in Angstrom^2, time is in ps
# D = slope / 6 in units of Angstrom^2/ps
D_A2_ps = slope / 6.0

# Convert to m^2/s
# 1 Angstrom = 1e-10 m
# 1 ps = 1e-12 s
# So 1 A^2/ps = 1e-20 m^2 / 1e-12 s = 1e-8 m^2/s
D_m2_s = D_A2_ps * 1e-8

print(f"Linear fit range: {time_fit[0]:.2f} ps to {time_fit[-1]:.2f} ps")
print(f"Slope: {slope:.6f} A^2/ps")
print(f"R^2: {r_value**2:.6f}")
print(f"Diffusion coefficient: {D_A2_ps:.6f} A^2/ps")
print(f"Diffusion coefficient: {D_m2_s:.6e} m^2/s")
print(f"\nFinal answer (in m^2/s): {D_m2_s:.2e}")

# Plot MSD vs time
plt.figure(figsize=(10, 6))
plt.plot(time_ps, msd, 'b-', linewidth=1, label='MSD data')
plt.plot(time_fit, slope * time_fit + intercept, 'r--', linewidth=2, 
         label=f'Linear fit (R²={r_value**2:.4f})')
plt.xlabel('Time (ps)', fontsize=12)
plt.ylabel('MSD (Ų)', fontsize=12)
plt.title(f'Mean Squared Displacement at 2500K\nD = {D_m2_s:.2e} m²/s', fontsize=14)
plt.legend(fontsize=10)
plt.grid(true, alpha=0.3)
plt.tight_layout()
plt.savefig('msd_plot.png', dpi=150)
print("\nPlot saved as msd_plot.png")

# LAMMPS input script for silicon melting and diffusion coefficient calculation
# Task: Heat silicon from 300K to 2500K and calculate diffusion coefficient

# Initialization
units           metal
atom_style      full
boundary        p p p

# Read structure and replicate
read_data       si_structure.data
replicate       3 3 3

# Define potential - Stillinger-Weber for Si
pair_style      sw
pair_coeff      * * /potentials/SW/Si.sw Si

# Neighbor settings
neighbor        2.0 bin
neigh_modify    every 1 delay 0 check yes

# Timestep
timestep        0.001  # 1 fs

# Thermodynamic output
thermo          1000
thermo_style    custom step temp press density pe ke etotal vol

# Stage 1: Initial equilibration at 300K (brief)
velocity        all create 300.0 12345 dist gaussian
fix             1 all npt temp 300.0 300.0 0.1 iso 0.0 0.0 1.0
run             10000  # 10 ps initial equilibration
unfix           1

# Stage 2: Heating from 300K to 2500K at 2.2 K/ps
# Heating time: (2500-300)/2.2 = 1000 ps = 1,000,000 steps
fix             2 all npt temp 300.0 2500.0 0.1 iso 0.0 0.0 1.0
run             1000000
unfix           2

# Stage 3: Equilibration at 2500K for 500 ps with MSD calculation
reset_timestep  0

# Compute MSD
compute         msd all msd com yes

# Output MSD data
fix             3 all npt temp 2500.0 2500.0 0.1 iso 0.0 0.0 1.0
fix             msd_output all print 1000 "$(step) $(c_msd[1]) $(c_msd[2]) $(c_msd[3]) $(c_msd[4])" file msd_data.txt screen no title "# step msd_x msd_y msd_z msd_total"

thermo          1000
thermo_style    custom step temp press density pe ke etotal vol c_msd[4]

run             500000  # 500 ps equilibration

print           "Simulation completed successfully"

#!/usr/bin/env python3
import numpy as np
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
from scipy import stats

# Read MSD data
data = np.loadtxt('msd_data.txt', comments='#')
steps = data[:, 0]
msd_total = data[:, 4]  # Total MSD (4th column)

# Convert steps to time (timestep = 0.001 ps)
timestep = 0.001  # ps
time = steps * timestep  # ps

print(f"Total data points: {len(time)}")
print(f"Time range: {time[0]:.2f} to {time[-1]:.2f} ps")
print(f"MSD range: {msd_total[0]:.4f} to {msd_total[-1]:.4f} Å²")

# Plot MSD vs time to visualize
plt.figure(figsize=(10, 6))
plt.plot(time, msd_total, 'b-', linewidth=0.5, alpha=0.7)
plt.xlabel('Time (ps)')
plt.ylabel('MSD (Ų)')
plt.title('Mean Squared Displacement vs Time')
plt.grid(true, alpha=0.3)
plt.savefig('msd_plot.png', dpi=150, bbox_inches='tight')
print("MSD plot saved as msd_plot.png")

# Calculate diffusion coefficient using Einstein relation: MSD = 6*D*t
# We'll use the linear regime - typically after initial transient
# Let's use the second half of the data for fitting to ensure we're in the diffusive regime
start_idx = len(time) // 2
time_fit = time[start_idx:]
msd_fit = msd_total[start_idx:]

print(f"\nUsing data from {time_fit[0]:.2f} to {time_fit[-1]:.2f} ps for fitting")

# Linear regression: MSD = 6*D*t
# slope = 6*D
slope, intercept, r_value, p_value, std_err = stats.linregress(time_fit, msd_fit)

print(f"\nLinear fit results:")
print(f"Slope: {slope:.6f} Ų/ps")
print(f"Intercept: {intercept:.6f} Ų")
print(f"R²: {r_value**2:.6f}")
print(f"Standard error: {std_err:.6e}")

# Calculate diffusion coefficient
# D = slope / 6
D_angstrom_ps = slope / 6.0  # Ų/ps

print(f"\nDiffusion coefficient:")
print(f"D = {D_angstrom_ps:.6e} Ų/ps")

# Convert to m²/s
# 1 Å = 1e-10 m, so 1 Ų = 1e-20 m²
# 1 ps = 1e-12 s
# D(m²/s) = D(Ų/ps) × (1e-20 m²/Ų) / (1e-12 s/ps) = D(Ų/ps) × 1e-8
D_m2_s = D_angstrom_ps * 1e-8

print(f"D = {D_m2_s:.6e} m²/s")

# Plot with fit line
plt.figure(figsize=(10, 6))
plt.plot(time, msd_total, 'b-', linewidth=0.5, alpha=0.5, label='MSD data')
plt.plot(time_fit, slope * time_fit + intercept, 'r-', linewidth=2, 
         label=f'Linear fit (R²={r_value**2:.4f})')
plt.xlabel('Time (ps)')
plt.ylabel('MSD (Ų)')
plt.title(f'MSD vs Time with Linear Fit\nD = {D_m2_s:.3e} m²/s')
plt.legend()
plt.grid(true, alpha=0.3)
plt.savefig('msd_fit_plot.png', dpi=150, bbox_inches='tight')
print("\nFit plot saved as msd_fit_plot.png")

# Save result to file
with open('diffusion_coefficient.txt', 'w') as f:
    f.write(f"Diffusion coefficient of liquid silicon at 2500K\n")
    f.write(f"D = {D_m2_s:.6e} m²/s\n")
    f.write(f"D = {D_angstrom_ps:.6e} Ų/ps\n")
    f.write(f"\nFit details:\n")
    f.write(f"Slope: {slope:.6f} Ų/ps\n")
    f.write(f"R²: {r_value**2:.6f}\n")
    f.write(f"Time range used: {time_fit[0]:.2f} to {time_fit[-1]:.2f} ps\n")

print("\nResults saved to diffusion_coefficient.txt")
print(f"\n{'='*60}")
print(f"FINAL RESULT: {D_m2_s:.6e} m²/s")
print(f"{'='*60}")

run 500000

undump msd_dump

print "Simulation completed successfully"

# LAMMPS input script for silicon melting and diffusion coefficient calculation
# Task: Heat silicon from 300K to 2500K, equilibrate, and compute diffusion coefficient

# Initialization
units metal
atom_style full
boundary p p p

# Read structure and replicate
read_data si_structure.data
replicate 3 3 3

# Define potential (Stillinger-Weber)
pair_style sw
pair_coeff * * /potentials/SW/Si.sw Si

# Set neighbor list
neighbor 2.0 bin
neigh_modify every 1 delay 0 check yes

# Thermodynamic output settings
thermo 1000
thermo_style custom step temp press density pe ke etotal vol

# Stage 1: Initial energy minimization
min_style cg
minimize 1.0e-6 1.0e-8 10000 100000

# Reset timestep and initialize velocities at 300K
reset_timestep 0
velocity all create 300.0 12345 dist gaussian

# Stage 2: Heating from 300K to 2500K at 2.2 K/ps
# Heating time: (2500-300)/2.2 = 1000 ps
# Timestep: 0.001 ps = 1 fs
timestep 0.001

# NPT ensemble for heating (zero pressure)
fix npt_heat all npt temp 300.0 2500.0 0.1 iso 0.0 0.0 1.0

# Run heating for 1000 ps = 1,000,000 steps
run 1000000

# Unfix heating
unfix npt_heat

# Reset timestep for equilibration
reset_timestep 0

# Stage 3: Equilibration at 2500K for 500 ps
fix npt_equil all npt temp 2500.0 2500.0 0.1 iso 0.0 0.0 1.0

# Run equilibration for 500 ps = 500,000 steps
run 500000

# Unfix equilibration
unfix npt_equil

# Reset timestep for MSD calculation
reset_timestep 0

# Stage 4: Production run for MSD calculation at 2500K
# Continue NPT at 2500K and compute MSD
fix npt_prod all npt temp 2500.0 2500.0 0.1 iso 0.0 0.0 1.0

# Compute MSD for all atoms
compute msd_all all msd com yes

# Output MSD data
fix msd_output all print 100 "$(step) $(c_msd_all[1]) $(c_msd_all[2]) $(c_msd_all[3]) $(c_msd_all[4])" file msd_data.txt screen no title "# Step MSD_x MSD_y MSD_z MSD_total"

# Run production for another 500 ps = 500,000 steps
run 500000

print "Simulation completed successfully"

# Initialization
units metal

read_data silicon.data

replicate 3 3 3

import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
from scipy import stats

# Read MSD data
data = np.loadtxt('msd.dat', skiprows=2)

# Extract columns
timesteps = data[:, 0]
msd_total = data[:, 4]  # Total MSD in Angstrom^2

# Convert timesteps to time in picoseconds
# timestep = 0.001 ps, and data is saved every 100 steps
time_ps = timesteps * 0.001  # time in ps

# Plot MSD vs time to visualize
plt.figure(figsize=(10, 6))
plt.plot(time_ps, msd_total, 'b-', linewidth=1, label='MSD data')
plt.xlabel('Time (ps)', fontsize=12)
plt.ylabel('MSD (Å²)', fontsize=12)
plt.title('Mean Squared Displacement vs Time', fontsize=14)
plt.grid(True, alpha=0.3)
plt.legend()
plt.savefig('msd_plot.png', dpi=150, bbox_inches='tight')
plt.close()

# For diffusion coefficient calculation, we need to fit the linear region
# The Einstein relation: MSD = 6*D*t
# So D = slope / 6

# Skip initial transient and use the linear region
# Let's use data from 50 ps onwards (after initial equilibration)
start_time = 50.0  # ps
mask = time_ps >= start_time

time_fit = time_ps[mask]
msd_fit = msd_total[mask]

# Perform linear regression
slope, intercept, r_value, p_value, std_err = stats.linregress(time_fit, msd_fit)

print(f"Linear fit results:")
print(f"  Slope: {slope:.6f} Å²/ps")
print(f"  Intercept: {intercept:.6f} Å²")
print(f"  R²: {r_value**2:.6f}")
print(f"  Standard error: {std_err:.6e}")

# Calculate diffusion coefficient
# D = slope / 6
# slope is in Å²/ps
# Convert to m²/s:
# 1 Å² = 1e-20 m²
# 1 ps = 1e-12 s
# So Å²/ps = 1e-20 / 1e-12 m²/s = 1e-8 m²/s

D_angstrom_ps = slope / 6.0
D_m2_s = D_angstrom_ps * 1e-8

print(f"\nDiffusion coefficient:")
print(f"  D = {D_angstrom_ps:.6f} Å²/ps")
print(f"  D = {D_m2_s:.6e} m²/s")

# Plot with fit
plt.figure(figsize=(10, 6))
plt.plot(time_ps, msd_total, 'b-', linewidth=1, label='MSD data', alpha=0.7)
plt.plot(time_fit, slope * time_fit + intercept, 'r--', linewidth=2, 
         label=f'Linear fit (t ≥ {start_time} ps)\nSlope = {slope:.3f} Å²/ps\nR² = {r_value**2:.4f}')
plt.xlabel('Time (ps)', fontsize=12)
plt.ylabel('MSD (Å²)', fontsize=12)

# LAMMPS input script for silicon melting and diffusion coefficient calculation
# Units: metal (eV, Angstroms, ps, etc.)

# Initialization
units           metal
atom_style      full
boundary        p p p

# Read structure and replicate
read_data       silicon.data
replicate       3 3 3

# Define potential - Stillinger-Weber
pair_style      sw
pair_coeff      * * /potentials/SW/Si.sw Si

# Define groups
group           all type 1

# Timestep
timestep        0.001  # 1 fs = 0.001 ps

# Thermodynamic output
thermo          1000
thermo_style    custom step temp press density pe ke etotal vol

# Stage 1: Initial equilibration at 300K (short)
velocity        all create 300.0 12345 dist gaussian
fix             1 all npt temp 300.0 300.0 0.1 iso 0.0 0.0 1.0
run             10000  # 10 ps initial equilibration
unfix           1

# Stage 2: Heating from 300K to 2500K at 2.2 K/ps
# Heating time = (2500-300)/2.2 = 1000 ps = 1,000,000 steps
fix             2 all npt temp 300.0 2500.0 0.1 iso 0.0 0.0 1.0
run             1000000  # 1000 ps heating
unfix           2

# Stage 3: Equilibration at 2500K for 500 ps
fix             3 all npt temp 2500.0 2500.0 0.1 iso 0.0 0.0 1.0
run             500000  # 500 ps equilibration
unfix           3

# Stage 4: Production run at 2500K with MSD calculation
# Reset time origin for MSD calculation
reset_timestep  0

# Compute MSD
compute         msd all msd

# Variables for output
variable        step_var equal step
variable        msd_x equal c_msd[1]
variable        msd_y equal c_msd[2]
variable        msd_z equal c_msd[3]
variable        msd_total equal c_msd[4]

# Output MSD data
fix             4 all npt temp 2500.0 2500.0 0.1 iso 0.0 0.0 1.0
fix             msd_output all print 100 "${step_var} ${msd_x} ${msd_y} ${msd_z} ${msd_total}" &
                file msd_data.txt screen no title "# step msd_x msd_y msd_z msd_total"

thermo          1000
thermo_style    custom step temp press density pe ke etotal vol c_msd[4]

# Run for another 500 ps to collect MSD data
run             500000  # 500 ps production run

unfix           4
unfix           msd_output

print           "Simulation completed successfully"

time_ps = timesteps * 0.001  # time in ps

plt.figure(figsize=(10, 6))
plt.plot(time_ps, msd_total, 'b-', linewidth=1, label='MSD data')

plt.grid(true, alpha=0.3)
plt.legend()
plt.savefig('msd_plot.png', dpi=150, bbox_inches='tight')
plt.close()

# For diffusion coefficient calculation, we need to fit the linear region
# The Einstein relation: MSD = 6*D*t
# So D = slope / 6

# Skip initial transient and use the linear region
# Let's use data from 50 ps onwards (after initial equilibration)
start_time = 50.0  # ps
mask = time_ps >= start_time

print(f"  R²: {r_value**2:.6f}")
print(f"  Standard error: {std_err:.6e}")

print(f"\nDiffusion coefficient:")
print(f"  D = {D_angstrom_ps:.6f} Å²/ps")
print(f"  D = {D_m2_s:.6e} m²/s")

# Plot with fit
plt.figure(figsize=(10, 6))
plt.plot(time_ps, msd_total, 'b-', linewidth=1, label='MSD data', alpha=0.7)
plt.plot(time_fit, slope * time_fit + intercept, 'r--', linewidth=2, 
         label=f'Linear fit (t ≥ {start_time} ps)\nSlope = {slope:.3f} Å²/ps\nR² = {r_value**2:.4f}')
plt.xlabel('Time (ps)', fontsize=12)
plt.ylabel('MSD (Å²)', fontsize=12)
plt.title('Mean Squared Displacement vs Time with Linear Fit', fontsize=14)
plt.grid(true, alpha=0.3)
plt.legend(fontsize=10)
plt.savefig('msd_plot_with_fit.png', dpi=150, bbox_inches='tight')
plt.close()

print(f"\nPlots saved as 'msd_plot.png' and 'msd_plot_with_fit.png'")

# Save result to file
with open('diffusion_coefficient.txt', 'w') as f:
    f.write(f"Diffusion coefficient of liquid silicon at 2500K\n")
    f.write(f"=========================================\n")
    f.write(f"D = {D_m2_s:.6e} m²/s\n")
    f.write(f"\nFit details:\n")
    f.write(f"  Slope: {slope:.6f} Å²/ps\n")
    f.write(f"  R²: {r_value**2:.6f}\n")
    f.write(f"  Fit range: {start_time} - {time_ps[-1]:.1f} ps\n")

print(f"\nResult saved to 'diffusion_coefficient.txt'")
print(f"\n{'='*50}")
print(f"FINAL ANSWER: {D_m2_s:.2e}")
print(f"{'='*50}")

D_angstrom2_per_ps = slope / 6.0

}

units metal
atom_style full
boundary p p p

replicate 3 3 3

pair_style sw

neigh_modify every 1 delay 0 check yes

compute mytemp all temp

Start from a crystalline silicon structure, which is replicated three times in each direction. The Stillinger-Weber (SW) potential should be used to describe interatomic interactions. Perform the heating and equilibration under zero external isotropic pressure control using NPT ensemble. Heat the system from 300K to 2500K at a rate of 2.2 K/ps, then equilibrate the liquid for 500 ps. Use the Einstein relation to compute the diffusion coefficient from the mean squared displacement (MSD) data. Report the diffusion coefficient in units of m²/s.

import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
from scipy import stats

# Read MSD data
data = np.loadtxt('msd_data.txt', comments='#')
steps = data[:, 0]
msd_total = data[:, 4]  # Total MSD

# Convert steps to time (ps)
# Timestep is 0.001 ps, output every 100 steps
time = steps * 0.001  # in picoseconds

# Plot MSD vs time
plt.figure(figsize=(10, 6))
plt.plot(time, msd_total, 'b-', linewidth=1, alpha=0.7)
plt.xlabel('Time (ps)', fontsize=12)
plt.ylabel('MSD (Ų)', fontsize=12)
plt.title('Mean Squared Displacement vs Time at 2500K', fontsize=14)
plt.grid(True, alpha=0.3)
plt.savefig('msd_plot.png', dpi=150, bbox_inches='tight')
plt.close()

# For diffusion coefficient, use the linear region
# Typically use the latter half of the data to ensure linear regime
start_idx = len(time) // 2
time_fit = time[start_idx:]
msd_fit = msd_total[start_idx:]

# Linear fit: MSD = 6*D*t (in 3D)
slope, intercept, r_value, p_value, std_err = stats.linregress(time_fit, msd_fit)

# Calculate diffusion coefficient
# D = slope / 6 (Einstein relation in 3D)
D_angstrom_ps = slope / 6.0

# Convert to m²/s
# 1 Ų/ps = 1e-20 m² / 1e-12 s = 1e-8 m²/s
D_m2_s = D_angstrom_ps * 1e-8

print(f"\n=== Diffusion Coefficient Analysis ===")
print(f"Linear fit performed on time range: {time_fit[0]:.2f} - {time_fit[-1]:.2f} ps")
print(f"Number of data points used: {len(time_fit)}")
print(f"Slope: {slope:.6f} Ų/ps")
print(f"R²: {r_value**2:.6f}")
print(f"\nDiffusion coefficient (D):")
print(f"  {D_angstrom_ps:.6e} Ų/ps")
print(f"  {D_m2_s:.6e} m²/s")
print(f"\nFinal answer: {D_m2_s:.2e}")

# Plot with fit
plt.figure(figsize=(10, 6))
plt.plot(time, msd_total, 'b-', linewidth=1, alpha=0.5, label='MSD data')
plt.plot(time_fit, slope * time_fit + intercept, 'r-', linewidth=2, 
         label=f'Linear fit (R²={r_value**2:.4f})')
plt.xlabel('Time (ps)', fontsize=12)
plt.ylabel('MSD (Ų)', fontsize=12)
plt.title(f'MSD Analysis: D = {D_m2_s:.2e} m²/s', fontsize=14)
plt.legend(fontsize=10)
plt.grid(True, alpha=0.3)
plt.savefig('msd_fit_plot.png', dpi=150, bbox_inches='tight')
plt.close()

print("\nPlots saved: msd_plot.png, msd_fit_plot.png")

# Save result to file
with open('diffusion_coefficient.txt', 'w') as f:
    f.write(f"{D_m2_s:.2e}\n")
    f.write(f"\nDetailed results:\n")
    f.write(f"D = {D_m2_s:.6e} m²/s\n")
    f.write(f"D = {D_angstrom_ps:.6e} Ų/ps\n")
    f.write(f"Slope = {slope:.6f} Ų/ps\n")
    f.write(f"R² = {r_value**2:.6f}\n")

print("Result saved to: diffusion_coefficient.txt")
"}</action_input>

# LAMMPS input script for silicon melting simulation
# Task: Calculate self-diffusion coefficient at 2500K

# Initialization
units metal
atom_style full
boundary p p p

# Read structure
read_data si_structure.data

# Replicate 3x3x3
replicate 3 3 3

# Define potential - Stillinger-Weber
pair_style sw
pair_coeff * * /potentials/SW/Si.sw Si

# Neighbor settings
neighbor 2.0 bin
neigh_modify every 1 delay 0 check yes

# Compute temperature and pressure
compute myTemp all temp
compute myPress all pressure myTemp

# Thermodynamic output settings
thermo 1000
thermo_style custom step temp press density pe ke etotal vol

# Timestep
timestep 0.001

# Stage 1: Energy minimization
min_style cg
minimize 1.0e-6 1.0e-8 10000 100000

# Reset timestep after minimization
reset_timestep 0

# Stage 2: Heating from 300K to 2500K at 2.2 K/ps under NPT
# Heating time: (2500-300)/2.2 = 1000 ps = 1,000,000 steps
velocity all create 300.0 12345 dist gaussian
fix npt_heat all npt temp 300.0 2500.0 $(100.0*dt) iso 0.0 0.0 $(1000.0*dt)
run 1000000
unfix npt_heat

# Stage 3: Equilibration at 2500K for 500 ps under NPT
# Also compute MSD for diffusion coefficient calculation
reset_timestep 0
compute msd_compute all msd com yes
fix npt_equil all npt temp 2500.0 2500.0 $(100.0*dt) iso 0.0 0.0 $(1000.0*dt)

# Output MSD data
fix msd_output all print 1000 "$(step) $(c_msd_compute[1]) $(c_msd_compute[2]) $(c_msd_compute[3]) $(c_msd_compute[4])" &
    file msd_data.txt screen no title "# Step MSD_x MSD_y MSD_z MSD_total"

run 500000
unfix npt_equil
unfix msd_output

print "Simulation completed successfully"

# LAMMPS input script for silicon melting and diffusion calculation
# Units: metal (eV, Angstrom, ps, etc.)

units metal
atom_style full
boundary p p p

# Read structure and replicate 3x3x3
read_data silicon.data
replicate 3 3 3

# Define Stillinger-Weber potential
pair_style sw

# Neighbor settings
neighbor 2.0 bin

thermo_style custom step temp press density pe ke etotal vol c_msd_compute[4]

# Heating phase: 300K to 2500K at 2.2 K/ps

uncompute msd_compute
compute msd_compute all msd com yes

# Output MSD data every 100 steps for better statistics
fix msd_output all ave/time 100 1 100 c_msd_compute[4] file msd.dat

import numpy as np
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
from scipy import stats

# Read MSD data
data = np.loadtxt('msd_data.txt', comments='#')
steps = data[:, 0]
msd_total = data[:, 4]  # Total MSD

# Convert steps to time (ps)
# Timestep is 0.001 ps, output every 100 steps
time = steps * 0.001  # in picoseconds

# Plot MSD vs time
plt.figure(figsize=(10, 6))
plt.plot(time, msd_total, 'b-', linewidth=1, alpha=0.7)
plt.xlabel('Time (ps)', fontsize=12)
plt.ylabel('MSD (Ų)', fontsize=12)
plt.title('Mean Squared Displacement vs Time at 2500K', fontsize=14)
plt.grid(true, alpha=0.3)
plt.savefig('msd_plot.png', dpi=150, bbox_inches='tight')
plt.close()

# For diffusion coefficient, use the linear region
# Typically use the latter half of the data to ensure linear regime
start_idx = len(time) // 2
time_fit = time[start_idx:]
msd_fit = msd_total[start_idx:]

# Linear fit: MSD = 6*D*t (in 3D)
slope, intercept, r_value, p_value, std_err = stats.linregress(time_fit, msd_fit)

# Calculate diffusion coefficient
# D = slope / 6 (Einstein relation in 3D)
D_angstrom_ps = slope / 6.0

# Convert to m²/s
# 1 Ų/ps = 1e-20 m² / 1e-12 s = 1e-8 m²/s
D_m2_s = D_angstrom_ps * 1e-8

print(f"\n=== Diffusion Coefficient Analysis ===")
print(f"Linear fit performed on time range: {time_fit[0]:.2f} - {time_fit[-1]:.2f} ps")
print(f"Number of data points used: {len(time_fit)}")
print(f"Slope: {slope:.6f} Ų/ps")
print(f"R²: {r_value**2:.6f}")
print(f"\nDiffusion coefficient (D):")
print(f"  {D_angstrom_ps:.6e} Ų/ps")
print(f"  {D_m2_s:.6e} m²/s")
print(f"\nFinal answer: {D_m2_s:.2e}")

# Plot with fit
plt.figure(figsize=(10, 6))
plt.plot(time, msd_total, 'b-', linewidth=1, alpha=0.5, label='MSD data')
plt.plot(time_fit, slope * time_fit + intercept, 'r-', linewidth=2, 
         label=f'Linear fit (R²={r_value**2:.4f})')
plt.xlabel('Time (ps)', fontsize=12)
plt.ylabel('MSD (Ų)', fontsize=12)
plt.title(f'MSD Analysis: D = {D_m2_s:.2e} m²/s', fontsize=14)
plt.legend(fontsize=10)
plt.grid(true, alpha=0.3)
plt.savefig('msd_fit_plot.png', dpi=150, bbox_inches='tight')
plt.close()

print("\nPlots saved: msd_plot.png, msd_fit_plot.png")

# Save result to file
with open('diffusion_coefficient.txt', 'w') as f:
    f.write(f"{D_m2_s:.2e}\n")
    f.write(f"\nDetailed results:\n")
    f.write(f"D = {D_m2_s:.6e} m²/s\n")
    f.write(f"D = {D_angstrom_ps:.6e} Ų/ps\n")
    f.write(f"Slope = {slope:.6f} Ų/ps\n")
    f.write(f"R² = {r_value**2:.6f}\n")

print("Result saved to: diffusion_coefficient.txt")

import numpy as np
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
from scipy import stats

# Read the MSD data
data = np.loadtxt('msd.dat', skiprows=2)

# Extract time (in ps) and total MSD (in Angstrom^2)
# timestep is in femtoseconds, dt = 0.001 ps = 1 fs
timesteps = data[:, 0]
time_ps = timesteps * 0.001  # Convert timesteps to ps
msd_total = data[:, 4]  # Total MSD in Angstrom^2

# Plot MSD vs time to visualize
plt.figure(figsize=(10, 6))
plt.plot(time_ps, msd_total, 'b-', linewidth=0.5)
plt.xlabel('Time (ps)')
plt.ylabel('MSD (Angstrom^2)')
plt.title('Mean Squared Displacement vs Time')
plt.grid(true)
plt.savefig('msd_plot.png', dpi=150)
plt.close()

# For diffusion coefficient calculation, we need the linear regime
# Typically, we skip the initial ballistic regime and use the middle portion
# Let's use data from 50 ps to 450 ps (avoiding initial transient and final fluctuations)
start_idx = np.argmin(np.abs(time_ps - 50))
end_idx = np.argmin(np.abs(time_ps - 450))

time_linear = time_ps[start_idx:end_idx]
msd_linear = msd_total[start_idx:end_idx]

# Perform linear regression
slope, intercept, r_value, p_value, std_err = stats.linregress(time_linear, msd_linear)

print(f"Linear regression results (50-450 ps):")
print(f"Slope: {slope:.6f} Angstrom^2/ps")
print(f"Intercept: {intercept:.6f} Angstrom^2")
print(f"R^2: {r_value**2:.6f}")
print(f"Standard error: {std_err:.6f}")

# Calculate diffusion coefficient using Einstein relation: D = MSD / (6t)
# D = slope / 6
D_angstrom_ps = slope / 6.0

print(f"\nDiffusion coefficient: {D_angstrom_ps:.6f} Angstrom^2/ps")

# Convert to m^2/s
# 1 Angstrom^2/ps = 1e-20 m^2 / 1e-12 s = 1e-8 m^2/s
D_m2_s = D_angstrom_ps * 1e-8

print(f"Diffusion coefficient: {D_m2_s:.6e} m^2/s")
print(f"Diffusion coefficient (scientific notation): {D_m2_s}")

# Plot the linear fit
plt.figure(figsize=(10, 6))
plt.plot(time_ps, msd_total, 'b-', linewidth=0.5, label='MSD data', alpha=0.5)
plt.plot(time_linear, slope * time_linear + intercept, 'r-', linewidth=2, label=f'Linear fit (50-450 ps)\nSlope = {slope:.3f} Å²/ps')
plt.xlabel('Time (ps)')
plt.ylabel('MSD (Angstrom^2)')
plt.title('Mean Squared Displacement vs Time with Linear Fit')
plt.legend()
plt.grid(true)
plt.savefig('msd_with_fit.png', dpi=150)
plt.close()

print(f"\nPlots saved as 'msd_plot.png' and 'msd_with_fit.png'")
print(f"\nFinal answer: {D_m2_s:.2e}")

import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
from scipy import stats

data = np.loadtxt('msd_data.txt', comments='#')
steps = data[:, 0]
msd_total = data[:, 4]  # Total MSD

# Convert steps to time (ps)
# Timestep is 0.001 ps, output every 100 steps
time = steps * 0.001  # in picoseconds

# Plot MSD vs time
plt.figure(figsize=(10, 6))
plt.plot(time, msd_total, 'b-', linewidth=1, alpha=0.7)
plt.xlabel('Time (ps)', fontsize=12)
plt.ylabel('MSD (A^2)', fontsize=12)
plt.title('Mean Squared Displacement vs Time at 2500K', fontsize=14)
plt.grid(true, alpha=0.3)
plt.savefig('msd_plot.png', dpi=150, bbox_inches='tight')
plt.close()

# For diffusion coefficient, use the linear region
# Typically use the latter half of the data to ensure linear regime
start_idx = len(time) // 2
time_fit = time[start_idx:]
msd_fit = msd_total[start_idx:]

# Linear fit: MSD = 6*D*t (in 3D)
slope, intercept, r_value, p_value, std_err = stats.linregress(time_fit, msd_fit)

# Calculate diffusion coefficient
# D = slope / 6 (Einstein relation in 3D)
D_angstrom_ps = slope / 6.0

# Convert to m^2/s
# 1 A^2/ps = 1e-20 m^2 / 1e-12 s = 1e-8 m^2/s
D_m2_s = D_angstrom_ps * 1e-8

print(f"\n=== Diffusion Coefficient Analysis ===")
print(f"Linear fit performed on time range: {time_fit[0]:.2f} - {time_fit[-1]:.2f} ps")
print(f"Number of data points used: {len(time_fit)}")
print(f"Slope: {slope:.6f} A^2/ps")
print(f"R-squared: {r_value**2:.6f}")
print(f"\nDiffusion coefficient (D):")
print(f"  {D_angstrom_ps:.6e} A^2/ps")
print(f"  {D_m2_s:.6e} m^2/s")
print(f"\nFinal answer: {D_m2_s:.2e}")

# Plot with fit
plt.figure(figsize=(10, 6))
plt.plot(time, msd_total, 'b-', linewidth=1, alpha=0.5, label='MSD data')
plt.plot(time_fit, slope * time_fit + intercept, 'r-', linewidth=2, 
         label=f'Linear fit (R^2={r_value**2:.4f})')
plt.xlabel('Time (ps)', fontsize=12)
plt.ylabel('MSD (A^2)', fontsize=12)
plt.title(f'MSD Analysis: D = {D_m2_s:.2e} m^2/s', fontsize=14)
plt.legend(fontsize=10)
plt.grid(true, alpha=0.3)
plt.savefig('msd_fit_plot.png', dpi=150, bbox_inches='tight')
plt.close()

print("\nPlots saved: msd_plot.png, msd_fit_plot.png")

# Save result to file
with open('diffusion_coefficient.txt', 'w') as f:
    f.write(f"{D_m2_s:.2e}\n")
    f.write(f"\nDetailed results:\n")
    f.write(f"D = {D_m2_s:.6e} m^2/s\n")
    f.write(f"D = {D_angstrom_ps:.6e} A^2/ps\n")
    f.write(f"Slope = {slope:.6f} A^2/ps\n")
    f.write(f"R-squared = {r_value**2:.6f}\n")

# LAMMPS input script for silicon melting and diffusion coefficient calculation
# Units: metal (eV, Angstrom, ps, etc.)

units metal
atom_style full
boundary p p p

# Read structure and replicate
read_data silicon.data
replicate 3 3 3

# Define Stillinger-Weber potential
pair_style sw
pair_coeff * * /potentials/SW/Si.sw Si

# Neighbor list settings
neighbor 0.3 bin
neigh_modify delay 5 every 1

# Initialize velocities at 300K
velocity all create 300.0 12345 dist gaussian

# Thermodynamic output settings
thermo 1000
thermo_style custom step temp press density pe ke etotal vol

# Timestep (1 fs)
timestep 0.001

# Stage 1: Heating from 300K to 2500K at 2.2 K/ps under NPT (zero pressure)
# Time needed: (2500-300)/2.2 = 1000 ps = 1,000,000 steps
fix npt1 all npt temp 300.0 2500.0 $(100.0*dt) iso 0.0 0.0 $(1000.0*dt)
run 1000000
unfix npt1

# Stage 2: Equilibration at 2500K for 500 ps = 500,000 steps
# Also compute MSD for diffusion coefficient calculation
fix npt2 all npt temp 2500.0 2500.0 $(100.0*dt) iso 0.0 0.0 $(1000.0*dt)

# Reset time and compute MSD

# LAMMPS input script for silicon melting simulation
# Task: Calculate self-diffusion coefficient of liquid Si at 2500K

# Initialization
units           metal
atom_style      full
boundary        p p p

# Read structure and replicate
read_data       si_structure.data
replicate       3 3 3

# Define potential - Stillinger-Weber
pair_style      sw
pair_coeff      * * /potentials/SW/Si.sw Si

# Neighbor list settings
neighbor        2.0 bin
neigh_modify    every 1 delay 0 check yes

# Compute settings
compute         myTemp all temp
compute         myPress all pressure myTemp

# Thermo output settings
thermo_style    custom step temp press density pe ke etotal vol
thermo          1000

# ===== STAGE 1: Initial equilibration at 300K =====
velocity        all create 300.0 12345 dist gaussian
fix             1 all npt temp 300.0 300.0 0.1 iso 0.0 0.0 1.0
timestep        0.001
run             50000
unfix           1

# ===== STAGE 2: Heating from 300K to 2500K at 2.2 K/ps =====
# Heating time: (2500-300)/2.2 = 1000 ps = 1,000,000 steps
fix             2 all npt temp 300.0 2500.0 0.1 iso 0.0 0.0 1.0
run             1000000
unfix           2

# ===== STAGE 3: Equilibration at 2500K for 500 ps =====
fix             3 all npt temp 2500.0 2500.0 0.1 iso 0.0 0.0 1.0
run             500000
unfix           3

# ===== STAGE 4: Production run with MSD calculation =====
# Continue at 2500K and compute MSD for diffusion coefficient
reset_timestep  0
fix             4 all npt temp 2500.0 2500.0 0.1 iso 0.0 0.0 1.0

# Compute MSD
compute         msd all msd com yes

# Output MSD data using variable
variable        step_var equal step
variable        msd_x equal c_msd[1]
variable        msd_y equal c_msd[2]
variable        msd_z equal c_msd[3]
variable        msd_total equal c_msd[4]

fix             msd_output all print 1000 "${step_var} ${msd_x} ${msd_y} ${msd_z} ${msd_total}" &
                file msd_data.txt screen no title "# Step MSD_x MSD_y MSD_z MSD_total"

# Run for another 500 ps to collect MSD data
thermo          1000
run             500000

unfix           4
unfix           msd_output

#!/usr/bin/env python3
import numpy as np
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
from scipy import stats

# Read MSD data
data = np.loadtxt('msd_data.txt', comments='#')

# Extract columns: step, MSD_x, MSD_y, MSD_z, MSD_total
steps = data[:, 0]
msd_total = data[:, 4]

# Convert steps to time (ps)
# timestep = 0.001 ps = 1 fs
timestep = 0.001  # ps
time = steps * timestep  # ps

# Use data after initial transient (skip first 20% to ensure equilibration)
skip_fraction = 0.2
skip_points = int(len(time) * skip_fraction)

time_fit = time[skip_points:]
msd_fit = msd_total[skip_points:]

print(f"Total data points: {len(time)}")
print(f"Using {len(time_fit)} points for fitting (skipping first {skip_points} points)")
print(f"Time range for fitting: {time_fit[0]:.2f} - {time_fit[-1]:.2f} ps")

# Perform linear regression: MSD = 6*D*t
# slope = 6*D, so D = slope/6
slope, intercept, r_value, p_value, std_err = stats.linregress(time_fit, msd_fit)

print(f"\nLinear fit results:")
print(f"Slope: {slope:.6f} Å²/ps")
print(f"Intercept: {intercept:.6f} Å²")
print(f"R²: {r_value**2:.6f}")

# Calculate diffusion coefficient
D_angstrom_ps = slope / 6.0  # Å²/ps

# Convert to m²/s
# 1 Å² = 1e-20 m²
# 1 ps = 1e-12 s
# So 1 Å²/ps = 1e-8 m²/s
D_m2_s = D_angstrom_ps * 1e-8  # m²/s

print(f"\nDiffusion coefficient:")
print(f"D = {D_angstrom_ps:.6f} Å²/ps")
print(f"D = {D_m2_s:.6e} m²/s")

# Plot MSD vs time
plt.figure(figsize=(10, 6))
plt.plot(time, msd_total, 'b-', linewidth=0.5, label='MSD data')
plt.plot(time_fit, slope * time_fit + intercept, 'r--', linewidth=2, 
         label=f'Linear fit (slope={slope:.3f} Å²/ps, R²={r_value**2:.4f})')
plt.xlabel('Time (ps)', fontsize=12)
plt.ylabel('MSD (Å²)', fontsize=12)
plt.title(f'Mean Squared Displacement at 2500K\nD = {D_m2_s:.3e} m²/s', fontsize=14)
plt.legend(fontsize=10)
plt.grid(true, alpha=0.3)
plt.tight_layout()
plt.savefig('msd_plot.png', dpi=150)
print(f"\nPlot saved as msd_plot.png")

# Save the final result
with open('diffusion_coefficient.txt', 'w') as f:
    f.write(f"Diffusion coefficient of liquid silicon at 2500K\n")
    f.write(f"D = {D_m2_s:.6e} m²/s\n")
    f.write(f"D = {D_angstrom_ps:.6f} Å²/ps\n")
    f.write(f"\nLinear fit details:\n")
    f.write(f"Slope: {slope:.6f} Å²/ps\n")
    f.write(f"Intercept: {intercept:.6f} Å²\n")
    f.write(f"R²: {r_value**2:.6f}\n")
    f.write(f"Data points used: {len(time_fit)} (skipped first {skip_points})\n")
    f.write(f"Time range: {time_fit[0]:.2f} - {time_fit[-1]:.2f} ps\n")

print(f"\nResults saved to diffusion_coefficient.txt")
print(f"\nFinal answer: {D_m2_s:.6e}")

Great! I have the MSD data. Now I need to create a Python script to:
1. Read the MSD data
2. Calculate the diffusion coefficient using the Einstein relation: D = MSD / (6t)
3. The MSD data is in Angstrom^2 and time is in picoseconds (ps)
4. I need to convert the result to m²/s

The Einstein relation in 3D is:
MSD = 6Dt

So: D = MSD / (6t)

For units:
- MSD is in Angstrom^2 (Å²)
- Time is in ps
- Need to convert to m²/s

Conversion:
- 1 Å = 10^-10 m, so 1 Å² = 10^-20 m²
- 1 ps = 10^-12 s

So D (in m²/s) = MSD (Å²) / (6 * t (ps)) * 10^-20 / 10^-12 = MSD / (6*t) * 10^-8

Let me write a Python script to calculate this from the MSD data. I should use the linear region of the MSD vs time plot to get the most accurate diffusion coefficient.
</thought>

import matplotlib.pyplot as plt

# Read MSD data
data = np.loadtxt('msd_data.txt', skiprows=2)

# Extract time steps and MSD (4th column is total MSD)
steps = data[:, 0]
msd = data[:, 4]  # Total MSD

# Convert steps to time in ps (timestep = 0.001 ps)
time_ps = steps * 0.001

# Plot MSD vs time to visualize
plt.figure(figsize=(10, 6))
plt.plot(time_ps, msd, 'b-', linewidth=1)
plt.xlabel('Time (ps)', fontsize=12)
plt.ylabel('MSD (Angstrom^2)', fontsize=12)
plt.title('Mean Square Displacement vs Time', fontsize=14)
plt.grid(True, alpha=0.3)
plt.savefig('msd_vs_time.png', dpi=150, bbox_inches='tight')
plt.close()

# Use linear region for fitting (typically after initial transient)
# Let's use data from 10 ps onwards (step 10000 onwards)
start_index = np.where(steps >= 10000)[0][0]
time_fit = time_ps[start_index:]
msd_fit = msd[start_index:]

# Linear fit: MSD = 6Dt (slope = 6D)
coeffs = np.polyfit(time_fit, msd_fit, 1)
slope = coeffs[0]  # This is 6D in Angstrom^2/ps

# Calculate diffusion coefficient
# D = slope / 6 in Angstrom^2/ps
D_angstrom_ps = slope / 6.0

# Convert to m^2/s
# 1 Angstrom^2 = 10^-20 m^2
# 1 ps = 10^-12 s
# So D(m^2/s) = D(Angstrom^2/ps) * 10^-20 / 10^-12 = D(Angstrom^2/ps) * 10^-8
D_m2_s = D_angstrom_ps * 1e-8

print(f"Linear fit from {time_fit[0]:.1f} ps to {time_fit[-1]:.1f} ps")
print(f"Slope (6D): {slope:.6f} Angstrom^2/ps")
print(f"Diffusion coefficient: {D_angstrom_ps:.6f} Angstrom^2/ps")
print(f"Diffusion coefficient: {D_m2_s:.6e} m^2/s")
print(f"\nFinal answer: {D_m2_s:.2e}")

# Plot with fit
plt.figure(figsize=(10, 6))
plt.plot(time_ps, msd, 'b-', linewidth=1, label='MSD data')
plt.plot(time_fit, np.polyval(coeffs, time_fit), 'r--', linewidth=2, 
         label=f'Linear fit (D = {D_m2_s:.2e} m²/s)')
plt.xlabel('Time (ps)', fontsize=12)
plt.ylabel('MSD (Angstrom^2)', fontsize=12)
plt.title('Mean Square Displacement vs Time with Linear Fit', fontsize=14)
plt.legend(fontsize=10)
plt.grid(True, alpha=0.3)
plt.savefig('msd_with_fit.png', dpi=150, bbox_inches='tight')
plt.close()

# Save result to file
with open('diffusion_coefficient.txt', 'w') as f:
    f.write(f"Diffusion coefficient at 2500K:\n")
    f.write(f"D = {D_m2_s:.6e} m^2/s\n")
    f.write(f"\nFit details:\n")
    f.write(f"Linear fit range: {time_fit[0]:.1f} - {time_fit[-1]:.1f} ps\n")
    f.write(f"Slope (6D): {slope:.6f} Angstrom^2/ps\n")
    f.write(f"D = {D_angstrom_ps:.6f} Angstrom^2/ps\n")

print("\nResults saved to diffusion_coefficient.txt")
print("Plots saved to msd_vs_time.png and msd_with_fit.png")
"}</action_input>

Tool: get_potential_metadata
Description: Returns metadata from a known LAMMPS potential file given the file path. The metadata includes potential type, elements supported, and the LAMMPS-compatible pair style keyword. Raises an exception if the path is invalid or the potential file is not recognized.

This tool provides a quick and reliable way to identify the type and supported elements of a LAMMPS potential file based on its filename, after first verifying that the file path is accessible.
It eliminates the need to parse the often large and complex contents of potential files, which can exceed processing limits in many systems. The tool first validates that the provided file path is non-empty and then checks file accessibility using a remote file inspection call. If the file path is invalid or inaccessible, a FileNotFoundError is raised. If the file is accessible, the tool extracts the filename using pathlib and matches it against a predefined set of known potential files. For recognized files, it returns a structured metadata string describing the potential type, supported elements, and the LAMMPS pair style.
If the filename does not match any known potential, a ValueError is raised.

When to use: When to use this tool:
    - Use when you need to quickly determine the type, supported elements, or the LAMMPS pair style of a LAMMPS potential file based on its filename.
    - Use when you want to validate that a potential file path is accessible before using it in a simulation workflow.
    - Best suited for selecting an appropriate potential file for a specific molecular dynamics (MD) simulation without reading or parsing the full file contents.
    - Recommended for gaining a fast, structured overview of a potential file's applicability to specific element combinations or simulation scenarios.

How this tool works:
    - Validates that the input file path is non-empty
    - Checks file accessibility using a remote file inspection call
    - Extracts the filename from the provided path using pathlib
    - Matches it against a set of known potential filenames
    - Returns a structured metadata string for recognized files
    - Raises FileNotFoundError for invalid or inaccessible paths
    - Raises ValueError for unrecognized potential filenames

Workflow: Typical workflow integration:
    1.  Select or obtain the potential file paths that might be relevant to your simulation task. 
    2.  Use this tool to retrieve metadata for each potential file path. The tool will either return metadata or raise an exception if the path or filename is invalid. 
    3.  Based on the metadata returned, choose the appropriate potential file for your simulation setup, and run the simulation using the selected potential file and the tool `run_lammps`.
Arguments:
- file_path (str, required): Path to the potential file.
This is the path to a LAMMPS-compatible potential file. The file must be accessible, and its filename is used to determine metadata, so it must match one of the known potential filenames.

Tool: convert_structure_to_lammps_data
Description: Converts a CIF-format structure file into a LAMMPS data file using a specified atom style.

This tool converts a crystal structure provided in CIF format (as a file) into a LAMMPS-compatible data file. Internally, it reads the CIF structure file using pymatgen, transforms it into a Structure object, and then serializes it to a LAMMPS data format using the LammpsData class. It supports configurable atom styles such as "atomic" or "charge", allowing flexibility based on simulation requirements.
This enables seamless transformation of standardized crystallographic data into simulation-ready LAMMPS input files, streamlining the setup process for molecular dynamics workflows.

When to use: When to use this tool:
    - Use when you need to convert crystallographic structure data in CIF format into a LAMMPS-compatible `.data` file.
    - Best suited for setting up molecular dynamics simulations where LAMMPS is the engine, and structure data is sourced from databases like Materials Project or experimental CIFs.
    - Avoid when your structure data is already in LAMMPS format or requires extensive pre-processing (e.g., force field assignments).
    - Recommended for automating simulation pipelines that begin with standardized structural data and end in LAMMPS-ready input formats.

How this tool works:
    - The tool reads the `.cif` file using `pymatgen.core.Structure.from_file` to create a Structure object.
    - The `LammpsData.from_structure` function is called, using the chosen `atom_style` to format the atomic data accordingly.
    - The resulting LAMMPS data file is written to the path specified by `output_file`.
    - The tool does not apply force fields or assign charges explicitly; it assumes the structure is already complete and appropriate for the selected `atom_style`.

Workflow: Typical workflow integration:
    1.  Ensure you have a valid CIF file containing the crystallographic structure of the material you want to simulate. Use the tool `get_structure_from_mp_text` to obtain one. 
    2.  Use this tool to convert the CIF file into a LAMMPS data file by providing the path to the CIF file, the desired output file path, and the atom style (if different from the default "charge"). 
    3.  The resulting LAMMPS data file can be used directly in LAMMPS simulations, using the tool `run_lammps` to run the simulation.
Arguments:
- structure_path (str, required): Path to the CIF-format structure file.
Path to the file containing the crystallographic structure. This file is read and converted into a pymatgen `Structure` object internally before being serialized to LAMMPS data format.
- output_file (str, required): Path where the LAMMPS data file will be saved.
This is the destination file path where the generated LAMMPS-compatible data file will be written. The output file will contain the atomic positions, types, and other necessary information formatted for LAMMPS simulations.
- atom_style (str, optional, default: charge): Atom style to be used in the LAMMPS data file, defaults to "charge".
Specifies the LAMMPS atom style to use when formatting the data file. Common values include: - "atomic": Includes atomic positions and mass, no charges. - "charge": Includes atomic charges in addition to position and mass. The choice of style should match the `atom_style` directive in the LAMMPS input script. Defaults to "charge" if nothing provided. Valid values: "real", "metal", "si", "cgs", "electron", "micro", "nano", "full", "".

This parameter specifies the absolute or relative path to the input script used by LAMMPS. The script typically contains simulation settings such as atom style, force field parameters, boundary conditions, and compute directives. 5. Compute MSD to calculate diffusion coefficient using Einstein relation

Let me calculate the timesteps:
- Heating rate: 2.2 K/ps
- Temperature change: 2500K - 300K = 2200K
- Heating time: 2200K / 2.2 K/ps = 1000 ps
- With timestep of 1 fs (0.001 ps), heating needs: 1000 ps / 0.001 ps = 1,000,000 steps
- Equilibration: 500 ps / 0.001 ps = 500,000 steps

# Task: Calculate self-diffusion coefficient at 2500K

# Initialization
units metal
atom_style full
boundary p p p

# Read structure and replicate
read_data si_structure.data
replicate 3 3 3

# Define potential - Stillinger-Weber
pair_style sw
pair_coeff * * /potentials/SW/Si.sw Si

neighbor 2.0 bin
neigh_modify delay 0 every 1 check yes

# Define compute for MSD (will be used during equilibration)
compute msd_compute all msd com yes

# Timestep
timestep 0.001  # 1 fs

# Thermodynamic output
thermo 1000
thermo_style custom step temp press density pe ke etotal vol

# Temperature change: 2200K, Rate: 2.2 K/ps, Time: 1000 ps = 1,000,000 steps
velocity all create 300.0 12345 dist gaussian
fix npt_heat all npt temp 300.0 2500.0 $(100.0*dt) iso 0.0 0.0 $(1000.0*dt)
run 1000000
unfix npt_heat

run 500000
unfix npt_equil
unfix msd_output

print "Simulation completed successfully"

Perfect! I have the MSD data. Now I need to calculate the diffusion coefficient using the Einstein relation:

D = (1/6) * lim(t→∞) d<r²>/dt

Where <r²> is the mean squared displacement (MSD). In the linear regime, the MSD is proportional to time:
<r²> = 6Dt

So the slope of MSD vs time gives us 6D, and therefore D = slope/6.

I need to:
1. Extract the MSD data (column 4 is MSD_total)
2. Convert time from steps to actual time (timestep = 0.001 ps)
3. Fit a linear regression to the MSD vs time in the diffusive regime
4. Calculate D from the slope
5. Convert from Angstrom²/ps to m²/s

Let me write a Python script to do this analysis.
</thought>

import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
from scipy import stats

# Read MSD data
data = np.loadtxt('msd_data.txt', skiprows=1)
steps = data[:, 0]
msd_total = data[:, 4]  # Column 4 is MSD_total in Angstrom^2

# Convert steps to time in picoseconds
timestep = 0.001  # ps
time_ps = steps * timestep

# Plot MSD vs time to visualize
plt.figure(figsize=(10, 6))
plt.plot(time_ps, msd_total, 'b-', linewidth=0.5)
plt.xlabel('Time (ps)')
plt.ylabel('MSD (Angstrom²)')
plt.title('Mean Squared Displacement vs Time')
plt.grid(True, alpha=0.3)
plt.savefig('msd_vs_time.png', dpi=150, bbox_inches='tight')
plt.close()

# For diffusion coefficient calculation, we need the linear regime
# Typically, we skip the initial ballistic regime (first ~10-20% of data)
# and use the middle portion where MSD is linear with time

# Let's use data from 100 ps to 400 ps (middle portion, avoiding initial and final)
start_time = 100  # ps
end_time = 400    # ps

mask = (time_ps >= start_time) & (time_ps <= end_time)
time_fit = time_ps[mask]
msd_fit = msd_total[mask]

# Perform linear regression: MSD = 6*D*t + intercept
slope, intercept, r_value, p_value, std_err = stats.linregress(time_fit, msd_fit)

print(f"Linear fit statistics (time range: {start_time}-{end_time} ps):")
print(f"Slope: {slope:.6f} Angstrom²/ps")
print(f"Intercept: {intercept:.6f} Angstrom²")
print(f"R²: {r_value**2:.6f}")
print(f"Standard error: {std_err:.6f}")
print()

# Calculate diffusion coefficient
# D = slope / 6 (in Angstrom²/ps)
D_angstrom_ps = slope / 6.0

print(f"Diffusion coefficient:")
print(f"D = {D_angstrom_ps:.6e} Angstrom²/ps")

# Convert to m²/s
# 1 Angstrom = 1e-10 m
# 1 ps = 1e-12 s
# So 1 Angstrom²/ps = (1e-10)²/(1e-12) m²/s = 1e-8 m²/s
D_m2_s = D_angstrom_ps * 1e-8

print(f"D = {D_m2_s:.6e} m²/s")
print()

# Plot with fit line
plt.figure(figsize=(12, 6))

# Full data
plt.subplot(1, 2, 1)
plt.plot(time_ps, msd_total, 'b-', linewidth=0.5, label='MSD data')
plt.plot(time_fit, slope * time_fit + intercept, 'r-', linewidth=2, label=f'Linear fit (R²={r_value**2:.4f})')
plt.xlabel('Time (ps)')
plt.ylabel('MSD (Angstrom²)')
plt.title('Full MSD Data')
plt.legend()
plt.grid(True, alpha=0.3)

# Zoomed to fit region
plt.subplot(1, 2, 2)
plt.plot(time_fit, msd_fit, 'b-', linewidth=1, label='MSD data (fit region)')
plt.plot(time_fit, slope * time_fit + intercept, 'r-', linewidth=2, label=f'Linear fit')
plt.xlabel('Time (ps)')
plt.ylabel('MSD (Angstrom²)')
plt.title(f'Linear Regime ({start_time}-{end_time} ps)')
plt.legend()
plt.grid(True, alpha=0.3)

plt.tight_layout()
plt.savefig('msd_analysis.png', dpi=150, bbox_inches='tight')
plt.close()

print(f"Plots saved: msd_vs_time.png and msd_analysis.png")
print()
print(f"FINAL RESULT: D = {D_m2_s:.6e} m²/s")

# Save result to file
with open('diffusion_coefficient.txt', 'w') as f:
    f.write(f"Diffusion coefficient of liquid silicon at 2500K\n")
    f.write(f"============================================\n")
    f.write(f"D = {D_m2_s:.6e} m²/s\n")
    f.write(f"\n")
    f.write(f"Fit details:\n")
    f.write(f"Time range: {start_time}-{end_time} ps\n")
    f.write(f"Slope: {slope:.6f} Angstrom²/ps\n")
    f.write(f"R²: {r_value**2:.6f}\n")
"}</action_input>

import numpy as np
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
from scipy import stats

# Read MSD data
data = np.loadtxt('msd_data.txt', skiprows=1)
steps = data[:, 0]
msd_total = data[:, 4]  # Column 4 is MSD_total in Angstrom^2

# Convert steps to time in picoseconds
timestep = 0.001  # ps
time_ps = steps * timestep

# Plot MSD vs time to visualize
plt.figure(figsize=(10, 6))
plt.plot(time_ps, msd_total, 'b-', linewidth=0.5)
plt.xlabel('Time (ps)')
plt.ylabel('MSD (Angstrom²)')
plt.title('Mean Squared Displacement vs Time')
plt.grid(true, alpha=0.3)
plt.savefig('msd_vs_time.png', dpi=150, bbox_inches='tight')
plt.close()

# For diffusion coefficient calculation, we need the linear regime
# Typically, we skip the initial ballistic regime (first ~10-20% of data)
# and use the middle portion where MSD is linear with time

# Let's use data from 100 ps to 400 ps (middle portion, avoiding initial and final)
start_time = 100  # ps
end_time = 400    # ps

mask = (time_ps >= start_time) & (time_ps <= end_time)
time_fit = time_ps[mask]
msd_fit = msd_total[mask]

# Perform linear regression: MSD = 6*D*t + intercept
slope, intercept, r_value, p_value, std_err = stats.linregress(time_fit, msd_fit)

print(f"Linear fit statistics (time range: {start_time}-{end_time} ps):")
print(f"Slope: {slope:.6f} Angstrom²/ps")
print(f"Intercept: {intercept:.6f} Angstrom²")
print(f"R²: {r_value**2:.6f}")
print(f"Standard error: {std_err:.6f}")
print()

# Calculate diffusion coefficient
# D = slope / 6 (in Angstrom²/ps)
D_angstrom_ps = slope / 6.0

print(f"Diffusion coefficient:")
print(f"D = {D_angstrom_ps:.6e} Angstrom²/ps")

# Convert to m²/s
# 1 Angstrom = 1e-10 m
# 1 ps = 1e-12 s
# So 1 Angstrom²/ps = (1e-10)²/(1e-12) m²/s = 1e-8 m²/s
D_m2_s = D_angstrom_ps * 1e-8

print(f"D = {D_m2_s:.6e} m²/s")
print()

# Plot with fit line
plt.figure(figsize=(12, 6))

# Full data
plt.subplot(1, 2, 1)
plt.plot(time_ps, msd_total, 'b-', linewidth=0.5, label='MSD data')
plt.plot(time_fit, slope * time_fit + intercept, 'r-', linewidth=2, label=f'Linear fit (R²={r_value**2:.4f})')
plt.xlabel('Time (ps)')
plt.ylabel('MSD (Angstrom²)')
plt.title('Full MSD Data')
plt.legend()
plt.grid(true, alpha=0.3)

# Zoomed to fit region
plt.subplot(1, 2, 2)
plt.plot(time_fit, msd_fit, 'b-', linewidth=1, label='MSD data (fit region)')
plt.plot(time_fit, slope * time_fit + intercept, 'r-', linewidth=2, label='Linear fit')
plt.xlabel('Time (ps)')
plt.ylabel('MSD (Angstrom²)')
plt.title(f'Linear Regime ({start_time}-{end_time} ps)')
plt.legend()
plt.grid(true, alpha=0.3)

plt.tight_layout()
plt.savefig('msd_analysis.png', dpi=150, bbox_inches='tight')
plt.close()

print(f"Plots saved: msd_vs_time.png and msd_analysis.png")
print()
print(f"FINAL RESULT: D = {D_m2_s:.6e} m²/s")

# Save result to file
with open('diffusion_coefficient.txt', 'w') as f:
    f.write(f"Diffusion coefficient of liquid silicon at 2500K\n")
    f.write(f"============================================\n")
    f.write(f"D = {D_m2_s:.6e} m²/s\n")
    f.write(f"\n")
    f.write(f"Fit details:\n")
    f.write(f"Time range: {start_time}-{end_time} ps\n")
    f.write(f"Slope: {slope:.6f} Angstrom²/ps\n")
    f.write(f"R²: {r_value**2:.6f}\n")
